bull_bear.body:
- India's largest manufacturer of laboratory glassware with a 64-year legacy; 3 out of 4 laboratory glassware products in India bear the Borosil brand
- Portfolio breadth of over 4,500 specialized products / SKUs across four divisions, enabling cross-selling of integrated solutions to institutional clients
- NABL-accredited in-house calibration laboratory at Bharuch and QR-code / laser UID traceability on Class A products, differentiating in high-precision segments
- Distribution and service backbone - over 150 channel partners, four warehouses across India and 80+ sales ambassadors, supporting a consistently achieved 95% success rate in delivering products within 24 hours
- Integrated, locally manufactured process systems following the Goel Scientific acquisition, enabling design and fabrication of complex custom industrial-scale pilot plants and automated reaction systems
- Regulatory credentials in pharmaceutical packaging - passed rigorous global client audits, ISO Class 8 cleanroom and delamination-free USP Type I glass, supporting long-term supply contracts with global injectable manufacturers
- Skilled craft base of 100+ expert glassblowers plus 130+ design engineers and product management professionals at the Pune instrumentation centre
- Technical collaborations with global industry leaders, including a German partner for Ultra-Pure Water instruments, completing the Lab Water portfolio from distillation to purification
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input cost volatility and pricing pressure — Precision borosilicate glass manufacturing is energy-intensive; volatility in global energy prices and the cost of specialized raw glass tubing can exert pressure on gross margins. This is accentuated by intensifying competition from domestic unorganized players and established global manufacturers, which may sustain pricing pressure particularly in commoditized product segments. Mitigation cited: dual-fuel manufacturing capability, long-term price-locked vendor contracts and dynamic pricing mechanisms enabling timely cost pass-throughs.
- Vendor concentration and import dependency for critical raw materials — The Company depends on a limited pool of domestic and international suppliers for borosilicate glass tubing and soda lime glass used in Laboratory Glassware and Pharmaceutical Primary Packaging, with technological constraints in developing indigenous capability for complex components; this may impact supply continuity and cost stability. Mitigation cited: localization and backward integration, vendor base diversification and multi-vendor sourcing frameworks.
- Macroeconomic and supply-chain volatility — Global economic moderation, inflationary pressures, geopolitical tensions and trade disruptions may impact demand for laboratory equipment and affect raw material procurement and export logistics. Mitigation cited: supplier diversification, data-driven inventory buffers for critical components and localized component sourcing.
- Quality and regulatory compliance in stringently regulated end-markets — Serving pharmaceutical and clinical sectors demands strict adherence to evolving global standards including US FDA, ISO and ASTM; any quality lapse or compliance gap poses a severe risk to brand equity and client retention. Mitigation cited: enhanced internal audits, automated optical quality-check systems on the production line and continuous compliance with global ISO/ASTM and USP standards.
- Technology and innovation obsolescence risk — Rapid advancement in laboratory automation, digital integration and alternative materials may render existing products less competitive and lead to product obsolescence if continuous innovation and R&D investment is not maintained. Mitigation cited: sustained R&D and new product development, product-line expansion and continuous customer engagement and market research.
- Foreign exchange exposure — A growing export footprint alongside specialized import requirements - raw materials, stores and spares and capex payments - makes currency fluctuation a continuous financial risk. The MD&A cites structured financial hedging, forward contracts and natural hedges, while the Corporate Governance Report states the Company does not enter into derivative instruments for trading or speculative purposes and has not entered into any hedging arrangements, with unhedged foreign currency exposure as on 31st March 2026 disclosed in the notes.
- Customer consolidation and procurement pressure — Increasing consolidation among global pharmaceutical and chemical companies is leading to centralized procurement and higher bargaining power, potentially exerting downward pressure on pricing and contract terms.
- Demand cyclicality in end-user industries — Segments such as chemicals and industrial manufacturing are subject to cyclical demand patterns, which may impact customer capital expenditure on process equipment and laboratory infrastructure - the demand base for the Process Systems division, whose subsidiary GSGWL saw high-value project execution deferred to the next financial year.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Borosil Scientific Limited designs and manufactures 3.3 borosilicate laboratory glassware and consumables, benchtop laboratory instrumentation under the LabQuest brand, USP Type I glass ampoules and tubular vials for pharmaceutical primary packaging, and customised industrial glass process systems. It serves pharmaceutical, biotechnology, specialty chemical, agrochemical, food and nutrition, academic, research and environmental-science customers in India and exports to over 90 countries. The business is organised around four pillars - Laboratory Consumables, Laboratory Instrumentation, Pharmaceutical Primary Packaging and Process Systems - sold through a distributor network, digital procurement channels including the Government e-Marketplace, and long-term supply contracts with global injectable manufacturers.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Laboratory Glassware and Consumables:** Volumetric flasks, Reagent bottles, Measuring cylinders, Beakers, Pipettes, Burettes, Crystallizing dishes, Petri dishes, Conical flasks, Test tubes, Sample vials, Analytical vials, Filtration assemblies, Filter membranes, Filter paper, Soxhlet extractors, Sintered glassware, Quartz crucibles, Desiccators, Microcentrifuge tubes, Stoppers and adapters
- **Laboratory Instrumentation:** LabQuest, High-speed centrifuges, Bottle Top Dispensers, Digital Burettes, Vortex mixers, Magnetic stirrers, Water and Dry Baths, Nitrogen Estimation Systems, Kjeldahl digestion units, Glass Care solutions, Ultra-Pure Water instruments, Water distillation systems
- **Pharmaceutical Primary Packaging:** USP Type I glass ampoules, Tubular glass vials
- **Process Systems:** Mini-reactor systems, Jacketed bench setups for pilot studies, Industrial-scale borosilicate glass reactors, Precision distillation units, Peptide synthesizers, Large-scale glass process equipment
business.title: Products & brands

outlook.body:
- Move steadily toward high-value, technology-enabled scientific solutions - data-logging-equipped water baths and electrochemistry instruments that enable laboratory digitisation and traceability
- Complete the Lab Water portfolio from distillation to purification by entering Ultra-Pure Water instruments through a technical collaboration with a German partner
- Position as a homegrown, world-class scientific products manufacturer aligned with Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India, driving import substitution across pharmaceutical, chemical and defense sectors
- Build differentiation in high-precision segments through NABL-accredited calibration capabilities at Bharuch and QR-code-based traceability on Class A products
- Cross-sell the four divisions as a unified integrated ecosystem to institutional clients as the primary lever for margin expansion and sustained revenue growth
- Expand LabQuest instrumentation into high-growth liquid handling and automated analytics, with high-margin proprietary innovations designed at the Pune R&D centre
- Scale bespoke customized chemical synthesis equipment in Process Systems to capture India's specialty chemicals and API capex cycle
- Extend pharmaceutical packaging into adjacent higher-value formats - siliconized vials, prefilled syringes and glass cartridges for biologics and complex injectables
- Broaden the consumables portfolio into water analysis and filter papers, leveraging in-house filter paper production at Bharuch
- Deepen global reach beyond the existing 90+ country presence through global trade fairs, technical seminars and regional distribution networks, diversifying revenue and reducing geographic concentration risk
- Embed automation and digital control across operations - advanced SAP HANA modules, Salesforce-driven CRM and Industry 4.0 concepts on the factory floor - to reduce variability, improve yields, shorten changeover times and tighten working capital discipline
- Replicate the Bharuch plant's TPM practices selectively across other plants, using Bharuch as an internal benchmark following its TPM Significant Award
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Borosil Scientific has actively expanded domestic production capacity to meet surging domestic demand and growing export requirements. At the Nashik plant the Company invested in fully automated new vial manufacturing lines using robotic systems to improve precision, consistency and output; the facility also includes an ISO Class 8 clean room enabling it to meet stringent pharmaceutical packaging requirements. The Bharuch facility has been equipped to produce filter paper, strengthening the in-house consumables portfolio, and carries NABL-accredited calibration capability. The Company entered a technical collaboration with a German manufacturer of water systems, adding Ultra-Pure Water instruments so that the Lab Water portfolio now covers the full spectrum from distillation to purification. Integration of the acquired Goel Scientific has equipped engineering teams to design and fabricate complex custom industrial-scale pilot plants and automated reaction systems. The stated growth blueprint for FY 2026-27 and beyond targets four areas: expanding LabQuest into high-growth liquid handling and automated analytics with proprietary innovations designed at the Pune R&D centre; scaling bespoke customized chemical synthesis equipment in Process Systems; expanding pharmaceutical packaging manufacturing into adjacent higher-value segments including siliconized vials, specialized prefilled syringes and precise glass cartridges for biologic and complex injectable drugs; and enhancing the water analysis and filter-paper consumable range. Investment priorities are stated as capacity and capability expansion in lab consumables and LabQuest, targeted investments in pharma primary packaging lines for advanced injectables, and continued strengthening of Process Systems. Digital integration and Industry 4.0 concepts continue to be deployed on the factory floor, with advanced SAP HANA modules and a Salesforce-driven CRM; the Bharuch plant received the TPM Significant Award during the year and its TPM practices are being selectively replicated across other plants. Manufacturing footprint remains four plants - Bharuch (Gujarat), Pune and Nashik (Maharashtra) and Vadodara (Gujarat) - supported by four warehouses across India.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Outlook across all business verticals remains positive, with Laboratory Glassware and Consumables delivering steady volume growth through an established distributor network and growing digital procurement channels including the Government e-Marketplace
- LabQuest instrumentation is capturing significant market share by substituting expensive, hard-to-maintain imports with high-performance, serviceable domestic alternatives
- Process Systems is positioned to benefit from ongoing industrial capex in the chemical sector; Pharmaceutical Packaging benefits from long-term, high-volume supply contracts with global injectable manufacturers
- Domestic demand was the key growth driver during the year, supported by growth in Indian pharmaceutical, chemical, cement, food, feed, mining, dairy and biotechnology sectors, while export revenues remained muted due to external challenges in certain international markets
- Product and customer mix continued to improve with higher penetration of value-added instruments - patented Bottle Top Dispensers, Digital Burettes, Kjeldahl-method nutrition analysis range, specialized consumables and advanced process systems
- Lab consumables mix has evolved from largely standard volumetric glassware to specialized vials, advanced filtration assemblies and sintered and quartz ware; LabQuest has broadened from bench-top into sample preparation, digestion, distillation and life sciences
- New customer segments opened by the Government's E20 initiative and the national focus on soil testing
- 'China+1' supply-chain diversification and Make in India / PLI-driven domestic capital expenditure accelerate demand for LabQuest instrumentation and Process Systems
- Structural growth in biologics, complex generics, vaccines and personalized medicine raises demand for high-precision glassware, Type I tubular vials and primary packaging; rising vaccine export momentum backed by WHO and UNICEF procurement programmes
- Increasingly strict global environmental and food safety regulations mandate high-frequency testing, assuring recurring demand for laboratory consumables and analytical tools
- Increasing adoption of GLP-1 drugs positions Borosil Process Systems through its peptide synthesizers and reactor systems
- Over the next five years, growth is seen driven by stronger manufacturing capabilities, continued TPM-led improvement, product innovation, strategic global partnerships and expansion into emerging markets
- GSGWL recorded a significant improvement in order booking during FY 2025-26, though execution of certain high-value projects was deferred to the next financial year due to factors beyond its control; management remains focused on timely execution of the order book
- Pharmaceutical Packaging arm benefits from long-term, high-volume supply contracts with global injectable manufacturers

currentContext.expansion: Borosil Scientific has actively expanded domestic production capacity to meet surging domestic demand and growing export requirements. At the Nashik plant the Company invested in fully automated new vial manufacturing lines using robotic systems to improve precision, consistency and output; the facility also includes an ISO Class 8 clean room enabling it to meet stringent pharmaceutical packaging requirements. The Bharuch facility has been equipped to produce filter paper, strengthening the in-house consumables portfolio, and carries NABL-accredited calibration capability. The Company entered a technical collaboration with a German manufacturer of water systems, adding Ultra-Pure Water instruments so that the Lab Water portfolio now covers the full spectrum from distillation to purification. Integration of the acquired Goel Scientific has equipped engineering teams to design and fabricate complex custom industrial-scale pilot plants and automated reaction systems. The stated growth blueprint for FY 2026-27 and beyond targets four areas: expanding LabQuest into high-growth liquid handling and automated analytics with proprietary innovations designed at the Pune R&D centre; scaling bespoke customized chemical synthesis equipment in Process Systems; expanding pharmaceutical packaging manufacturing into adjacent higher-value segments including siliconized vials, specialized prefilled syringes and precise glass cartridges for biologic and complex injectable drugs; and enhancing the water analysis and filter-paper consumable range. Investment priorities are stated as capacity and capability expansion in lab consumables and LabQuest, targeted investments in pharma primary packaging lines for advanced injectables, and continued strengthening of Process Systems. Digital integration and Industry 4.0 concepts continue to be deployed on the factory floor, with advanced SAP HANA modules and a Salesforce-driven CRM; the Bharuch plant received the TPM Significant Award during the year and its TPM practices are being selectively replicated across other plants. Manufacturing footprint remains four plants - Bharuch (Gujarat), Pune and Nashik (Maharashtra) and Vadodara (Gujarat) - supported by four warehouses across India.

risks.risk: Input cost volatility and pricing pressure
risks.note: Precision borosilicate glass manufacturing is energy-intensive; volatility in global energy prices and the cost of specialized raw glass tubing can exert pressure on gross margins. This is accentuated by intensifying competition from domestic unorganized players and established global manufacturers, which may sustain pricing pressure particularly in commoditized product segments. Mitigation cited: dual-fuel manufacturing capability, long-term price-locked vendor contracts and dynamic pricing mechanisms enabling timely cost pass-throughs.

risks.risk: Vendor concentration and import dependency for critical raw materials
risks.note: The Company depends on a limited pool of domestic and international suppliers for borosilicate glass tubing and soda lime glass used in Laboratory Glassware and Pharmaceutical Primary Packaging, with technological constraints in developing indigenous capability for complex components; this may impact supply continuity and cost stability. Mitigation cited: localization and backward integration, vendor base diversification and multi-vendor sourcing frameworks.

Global economic moderation, inflationary pressures, geopolitical tensions and trade disruptions may impact demand for laboratory equipment and affect raw material procurement and export logistics. Mitigation cited: supplier diversification, data-driven inventory buffers for critical components and localized component sourcing.

risks.risk: Quality and regulatory compliance in stringently regulated end-markets
risks.note: Serving pharmaceutical and clinical sectors demands strict adherence to evolving global standards including US FDA, ISO and ASTM; any quality lapse or compliance gap poses a severe risk to brand equity and client retention. Mitigation cited: enhanced internal audits, automated optical quality-check systems on the production line and continuous compliance with global ISO/ASTM and USP standards.

Rapid advancement in laboratory automation, digital integration and alternative materials may render existing products less competitive and lead to product obsolescence if continuous innovation and R&D investment is not maintained. Mitigation cited: sustained R&D and new product development, product-line expansion and continuous customer engagement and market research.

A growing export footprint alongside specialized import requirements - raw materials, stores and spares and capex payments - makes currency fluctuation a continuous financial risk. The MD&A cites structured financial hedging, forward contracts and natural hedges, while the Corporate Governance Report states the Company does not enter into derivative instruments for trading or speculative purposes and has not entered into any hedging arrangements, with unhedged foreign currency exposure as on 31st March 2026 disclosed in the notes.

Increasing consolidation among global pharmaceutical and chemical companies is leading to centralized procurement and higher bargaining power, potentially exerting downward pressure on pricing and contract terms.

Segments such as chemicals and industrial manufacturing are subject to cyclical demand patterns, which may impact customer capital expenditure on process equipment and laboratory infrastructure - the demand base for the Process Systems division, whose subsidiary GSGWL saw high-value project execution deferred to the next financial year.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Outlook across all business verticals remains positive, with Laboratory Glassware and Consumables delivering steady volume growth through an established distributor network and growing digital procurement channels including the Government e-Marketplace
- LabQuest instrumentation is capturing significant market share by substituting expensive, hard-to-maintain imports with high-performance, serviceable domestic alternatives
- Process Systems is positioned to benefit from ongoing industrial capex in the chemical sector; Pharmaceutical Packaging benefits from long-term, high-volume supply contracts with global injectable manufacturers
- Domestic demand was the key growth driver during the year, supported by growth in Indian pharmaceutical, chemical, cement, food, feed, mining, dairy and biotechnology sectors, while export revenues remained muted due to external challenges in certain international markets
- Product and customer mix continued to improve with higher penetration of value-added instruments - patented Bottle Top Dispensers, Digital Burettes, Kjeldahl-method nutrition analysis range, specialized consumables and advanced process systems
- Lab consumables mix has evolved from largely standard volumetric glassware to specialized vials, advanced filtration assemblies and sintered and quartz ware; LabQuest has broadened from bench-top into sample preparation, digestion, distillation and life sciences
- New customer segments opened by the Government's E20 initiative and the national focus on soil testing
- 'China+1' supply-chain diversification and Make in India / PLI-driven domestic capital expenditure accelerate demand for LabQuest instrumentation and Process Systems
- Structural growth in biologics, complex generics, vaccines and personalized medicine raises demand for high-precision glassware, Type I tubular vials and primary packaging; rising vaccine export momentum backed by WHO and UNICEF procurement programmes
- Increasingly strict global environmental and food safety regulations mandate high-frequency testing, assuring recurring demand for laboratory consumables and analytical tools
- Increasing adoption of GLP-1 drugs positions Borosil Process Systems through its peptide synthesizers and reactor systems
- Over the next five years, growth is seen driven by stronger manufacturing capabilities, continued TPM-led improvement, product innovation, strategic global partnerships and expansion into emerging markets
- GSGWL recorded a significant improvement in order booking during FY 2025-26, though execution of certain high-value projects was deferred to the next financial year due to factors beyond its control; management remains focused on timely execution of the order book
- Pharmaceutical Packaging arm benefits from long-term, high-volume supply contracts with global injectable manufacturers

- Move steadily toward high-value, technology-enabled scientific solutions - data-logging-equipped water baths and electrochemistry instruments that enable laboratory digitisation and traceability
